meta.title: Unit 5 — Simple Sentences (Test 7)
meta.subject: English Grammar
meta.description: Understand and identify the subject and predicate in simple sentences.

questions.question: Identify the subject in this sentence: 'The cat sings a song.'
questions.explanation: "The cat" is the subject. It is the person or thing the sentence is about.

questions.question: Identify the predicate in this sentence: 'My dog likes to draw.'
questions.explanation: "likes to draw" is the predicate. It tells what the subject is or does and contains the verb.

questions.question: In the sentence 'The teacher go to school every day,' the subject is 'The teacher'.
questions.explanation: Yes! "The teacher" is the subject because it tells who or what the sentence is about.

questions.question: In the sentence 'The cat sings a song,' the predicate is 'The cat'.
questions.explanation: No, "The cat" is the subject. The predicate is "sings a song" because it contains the verb and tells what the subject does.

questions.question: What does the subject of a sentence tell us?
options: Who or what the sentence is about
questions.explanation: The subject is the naming part of the sentence; it tells who or what performs the action or is being described.

questions.question: Every complete sentence must have both a subject and a predicate.
questions.explanation: Yes! A complete sentence needs both parts to express a complete thought: a subject (who/what) and a predicate (what they do/are).

questions.question: Identify the subject in this sentence: 'Tony plays soccer after school.' (Type the subject exactly as it appears)
questions.explanation: "Tony" is the subject because he is the person doing the action.

questions.question: Identify the predicate in this sentence: 'She reads a big book.' (Type the predicate exactly as it appears)
questions.explanation: "reads a big book" is the predicate because it starts with the verb "reads" and tells what "She" does.

questions.question: Sort each phrase fragment — is it a Subject or a Predicate?
questions.explanation: Subjects name the person or thing doing the action. Predicates tell what they do or are, starting with a verb.

questions.question: Sort each phrase fragment — is it a Subject or a Predicate?
questions.explanation: Subjects are the naming part (e.g. My cute puppy). Predicates are the telling part (e.g. runs very fast).

questions.question: Which predicate makes sense with the subject 'The hungry puppy'?
questions.explanation: "eats the dog food quickly" is a predicate that contains a verb and makes logical sense with the subject.

questions.question: Which subject makes sense with the predicate 'swims in the deep river'?
questions.explanation: "The little fish" is the subject that logically performs the action "swims in the deep river".

questions.question: In the sentence 'Mom cooks dinner,' the predicate is just the word 'dinner'.
questions.explanation: No! The predicate must contain the verb. The predicate is "cooks dinner," not just "dinner."

questions.question: Which of the following is a complete sentence?
options: The bird sings in the morning.
questions.explanation: "The bird sings in the morning" is complete because it has a subject ("The bird") and a predicate ("sings in the morning").

questions.explanation: Correct sentence: "The dog barks loudly."

questions.question: Arrange the words to form a correct sentence:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: "She reads a book every day."

questions.question: Which group of words contains BOTH a subject and a predicate?
options: My sister and her best friend
Likes to eat strawberry ice cream
My sister likes to eat strawberry ice cream.
questions.explanation: "My sister likes to eat strawberry ice cream." contains a subject ("My sister") and a predicate ("likes to eat strawberry ice cream").

questions.question: In the sentence 'The yellow duck swims in the pond,' what is the predicate? (Type the exact phrase)
questions.hint: Start with the verb 'swims' and write the rest of the sentence.
questions.explanation: The predicate is "swims in the pond" because it tells what the duck does.

questions.question: In the sentence 'The yellow duck swims in the pond,' what is the subject? (Type the exact phrase)
questions.hint: Write the naming part that comes before the verb 'swims'.
questions.explanation: The subject is "The yellow duck" because it tells who is swimming.
